Remix stages behave like exams. They quote pieces of the games just played and shuffle the order, so a cue learned on its own has to be recognized inside a crowd. Tsunku's music gives the cues their hooks, and Nintendo SPD builds the tiny scenes that make each hook visible.

The Japanese cartridge is the official release. Later games in the line traveled abroad on other hardware under the Rhythm Heaven name. This Advance original is where Karate Man, the night walk, and those remix exams began.
boktai-2-solar-boy-django:
San Miguel, a town Django can walk, anchors Boktai 2: Solar Boy Django. Konami released the sequel in 2004 with the sun sensor back in the cartridge, and his weapons are no longer limited to the solar gun. Swords, spears, and hammers can be carried, then fed with daylight so a blade still cares about the weather on the desk.

The Gun Del Sol is stolen at the start, which is why the other weapons exist. A glove that enchants ordinary steel with solar power lets him keep facing immortals until a gun can be recovered. Bright light still fills the meter; shade still starves any magic that depends on it.

Streets in San Miguel connect shops, a way to turn stored sunlight into money, and the roads out to the next dungeon. Forging can join two weapons into a stronger one when the solar work is done properly. Vampires remain the quarry, and a coffin still has to be handled after the fight ends.

Konami kept the physical sensor and widened combat past a single pistol. Someone who only played the first hunt will find a hometown, a missing gun, and a rack of melee weapons. Daylight on the cartridge still shapes the build, even when the thing in his hand is a sword.
mega-man-battle-network-6:
Cybeasts Gregar and Falzar split Mega Man Battle Network 6 into two cartridges, and Capcom shipped the pair in 2005 as the close of the original Battle Network story. Link Navis from earlier games join Lan once their crosses are earned. The cybeast tied to a given version changes which navis, chips, and last battles show up.

MegaMan.EXE still deletes viruses on the net while Lan operates him from the physical world. A Link Navi is playable machinery, not a portrait: after the cross is obtained, that navi can be operated and its attack brought into a folder. Gregar's roster and Falzar's roster do not match, so the two editions are a paired ending rather than copies.

Crosses alter MegaMan.EXE in a way the older Style Change system does not cover. Threads from the long netcrime saga meet the cybeasts here. Capcom treats the pair as the conclusion, with version-exclusive bosses standing in for one shared finale.

Operators who remember earlier navis see them return with actual battle roles. Picking Gregar or Falzar picks an ally list and picks the beast waiting at the end. The original story stops on this official pair.
dk-king-of-swing:
Donkey Kong hangs from pegs by gripping the shoulder buttons in DK: King of Swing. Paon developed the Game Boy Advance game, Nintendo published it in 2005, and holding L and R together is how he sticks. Release one side and he pivots; release at the right angle and he launches toward the next peg.

Boards of pegs sit in jungle scenery, with bananas and hazards in the gaps. A mistimed let-go drops him, and no run-and-roll replaces the swing. The mischief around the boards is jungle slapstick, but the buttons only ever mean grip, pivot, and throw.

Country games send him sprinting past barrels, mine carts, and long platforms. This cartridge barely uses that kind of running. Paon builds the test out of the peg field and the two shoulders, so a player who only mashes a jump will not cross the gap.

Nintendo published a jungle caper whose skill is the timing of a handhold. Charge the swing, choose a peg, and let go. The board itself, not a scrolling footrace, is the stage.
gunstar-super-heroes:
Treasure followed its Genesis shooter with a Game Boy Advance successor, Gunstar Super Heroes, and Sega published it in 2005. Europe knows that same cartridge as Gunstar Future Heroes. Shots can be pointed instead of locked forward, and weapon types merge into hybrid blasts the way the earlier Treasure guns could be combined.

Projectiles, mines, and oversized bosses crowd the screen. Choosing a merged weapon is a decision made before the room gets loud, and the adjustable aim puts the shot where the enemies actually stand. Treasure's dense patterns want movement and fire at the same time, with little empty space left to rest.

The Genesis Gunstar Heroes game is the ancestor, not a level list being squeezed onto a small panel. This Advance chapter continues those heroes on stages of its own, with the same appetite for crowded fire. Sega's publishing and the European Future Heroes name are official labels for that successor.

Two weapon traits together produce a blast neither trait manages alone. Aim that can leave the forward line matters once foes stop lining up in front of the barrel. Treasure stacks both ideas under a storm of moving objects so the handheld fight still feels like a Gunstar room.
tactics-ogre-the-knight-of-lodis:
Alphonse Loeher, a knight of the Lodis empire, is sent into a war on the island of Ovis in Tactics Ogre: The Knight of Lodis, the Game Boy Advance campaign Quest created, with Atlus publishing the English edition of that 2001 tale. Battles sit on an angled overhead grid where facing, height, and who can still act decide a skirmish. Class changes let a survivor study a new discipline after enough combat, so a spearman need not stay a spearman.

The campaign is a side story, separate from Let Us Cling Together and the struggle on Valeria. Noble houses on Ovis treat every truce as a pause between betrayals, and the knights caught in the middle have to decide which order to obey. A sour political choice can change who is still willing to fight in the next deployment.

Equipment and a class path belong to each character rather than to one avatar. Holding the high tiles and keeping a healer inside range matters as much as the printed attack number. A blocked lane can waste a spellcaster for a whole turn.

Quest designed the marches and the talk between them, and Atlus carried that script to English-speaking players. Clearing a map usually means protecting the units a later chapter still needs, rather than sprinting at the enemy leader.
mega-man-battle-network-3:
Programs placed in a Navi Customizer rewrite how the partner moves and shoots in Mega Man Battle Network 3, the White and Blue cartridges Capcom released in 2002. Style Change comes back, but the forms can be swapped instead of locking an operator into the first style earned. The WWW presses its plan through the net, while Lan's friendships keep pulling the plot back to people on the far side of the screen.

Parts that conflict can bug the Navi, so a strong setup is also a risk. Chip duels still occupy rows of panels, with a folder chosen before the fight and movement counted in squares. White and Blue differ in which chips and which encounters are easier to find, while the crisis itself stays the same shape.

Streets lead to jack-in ports, and the net beyond them is a chain of servers crossed on foot. Operators argue, pair up, and get cut off as the trouble moves from one district to the next. Lan's refusal to treat his Navi as a disposable tool sits under every virus fight.

Capcom built both cartridges around that net crisis and the friendships inside it. A style form changes favored chips and the look of the armor, so a folder that suited one form can feel clumsy after the switch.
super-mario-advance-4-super-mario-bros-3:
Physical e-Reader cards, scanned with the add-on accessory, supply extra courses alongside Super Mario Advance 4: Super Mario Bros. 3, Nintendo's 2003 handheld port of the NES world tour. The kings' stolen magic wands, the forked maps, and Bowser's airship still structure the main trip. A Mario Bros. battle mode shares the cartridge with that journey.

Those cards are objects you hold and swipe, a physical add-on kept beside the cart rather than a password typed on a title screen. Without the accessory, the eight worlds and their fortresses remain a full quest. Hammer suits, frog suits, and tanooki tails behave much as they did when the stages were new.

Some courses scroll on their own, some hide a second exit, and a few demand a very short hop onto a moving lift. Chain-link fences and pipes still ask for the older, stricter timing. The battle mode is the separate Mario Bros. arena, where foes are bumped from below on stacked platforms.

Nintendo issued the port in the Super Mario Advance line. The scanned-card stages widen the trip only when the matching cards and the e-Reader are both present.
mega-man-battle-network-5:
Occupied panels have to be won back one square at a time in Mega Man Battle Network 5, Capcom's 2004 pair sold as Team ProtoMan and Team Colonel. Each cartridge fields a different party of Navis for those operations. Lan and MegaMan remain the leads, while the allies standing on the map change with the version in the slot.

A liberation mission behaves more like a small tactics board than an ordinary chip duel. You step across darkened panels, free them, and only then confront the Navi holding the zone. Item cubes and enemy placements turn that advance into a route.

ProtoMan's roster and Colonel's roster do not match, which is why two carts were sold. A Navi's temperament shows up in the mission that Navi leads and in the chips that arrive with the alliance. The other version's team cannot be menu-swapped into your save.

Beneath the grid objectives, Capcom kept folders, row movement, and timed buster shots. Mail, keys, and distress calls in the city point toward the next liberation.
mega-man-battle-network-4:
Dark chips offer a harsher shortcut through the tournament brackets of Mega Man Battle Network 4, which Capcom shipped in 2003 as Red Sun and Blue Moon. Double Soul fusions let MegaMan borrow another Navi's form for a short run of altered shots. Lan travels from one official competition to the next while those chips keep tempting an easier clear.

The two versions exchange tournament lineups, souls, and scenario opponents rather than telling unrelated plots. Win a bracket and the tour shifts to another region with a fresh set of operators. Later cycles repeat matches with different details, so one folder has to survive more than a single pass.

A soul comes from a Navi Lan has already met, and the fusion changes elemental strengths plus the charge attack. Shaping the folder around that soul matters more than stuffing it with unrelated rare chips. Taking a dark chip raises the damage and feeds a corruption that is hard to set aside once it starts.

Towns between the arenas still hide small jobs and virus packs on the net. The tournament is the road the plot travels, with the chip trade running under the sanctioned matches.
ninja-five-o:
Joe Osugi's grappling rope does as much work as his sword in Ninja Five-O, the Hudson Soft side-scroller Konami published in the United States in 2003. He is a ninja police officer, and each building asks him to bring hostages out before the armed men finish the job. Europe received the same cartridge under the name Ninja Cop.

The camera stays in a strict side profile. The rope hooks beams and crates, swings him over gaps, and yanks a thug into a throw. Hostages have to be walked clear while the clock and the gunfire keep moving.

A sloppy swing drops him into a shot he cannot trade, and ordinary contact is already expensive. Shuriken cover the moments when a hook is the wrong tool. Learning a floor means knowing which beam is safe and which guard fires the instant he lets go.

Hudson Soft built the rooms, and Konami handled the American release of that strict rescue run. Later buildings add lasers, extra floors, and less time to pick the next hook.
advance-guardian-heroes:
Enn, Ray, and Hyu open Advance Guardian Heroes, Treasure's 2004 Game Boy Advance follow-up to the Saturn brawler, published by Ubisoft. Fire, lightning, and ice set those three starters apart, and directional weapon strings supply the combos. A demon's offer after a knockout can change which ending plays, a narrower fork than the many routes of the Saturn game.

Holding the attack and steering it changes the string, so one button is not the whole moveset. Launched foes can be chased upward, and a mistimed special leaves a wide opening. Magic spends a gauge that does not refill generously between crowds.

Stage order stays fixed, unlike the Saturn campaign's reshuffling paths. Two players can share story mode, and a versus option waits for a direct fight. Further fighters are earned later, but the campaign begins with the three elemental leads.

Ubisoft published Treasure's handheld brawler for players who never owned the Saturn original. Later chapters punish a repeated pattern, and mashing through a group stops working once the enemy sets overlap.
star-fox-64-3d:
Optional gyro aiming sits beside the medal routes in Star Fox 64 3D, Nintendo's 2011 stereoscopic remake of the rail shooter. Barrel rolls, charged lasers, and the wingmen's radio chatter return, with depth that pushes arches and debris toward the player. The edition in hand is the handheld remake, distinct from the original Nintendo 64 cartridge.

All-range sorties drop the Arwing into an open arena for certain bosses and planetary fights, apart from the on-rails corridors. Earning a medal on a stage opens the harder branch, so a sloppy run can miss the path toward another ending. Gyro aim can be switched off when the circle pad alone is preferred.

Peppy, Slippy, and Falco still call targets and still blunder into trouble you can prevent. A bomb clears a lane when the screen fills. Landmaster and submarine stretches remain among the route changes, along with returns to the Great Fox.

Nintendo kept the short-mission shape: pick a world, fly it, and watch the map redraw the next choices. Collecting every medal is its own task beside simply reaching one last boss.
tomodachi-life:
Songs, arguments, and clumsy dates fill the hours on the Mii island of Tomodachi Life, Nintendo's 2014 sandbox about neighbors rather than a scored contest. You feed them, choose their clothes, and assign apartments they promptly clutter. A face built from your own features can move in and start requesting snacks.

No results screen waits at the end of a tidy afternoon. Hunger, moods, and tiny errands call you back, and leaving a resident alone makes the complaint louder. Relationships form, collapse, and sometimes produce a child who then needs a room of their own.

Concerts, dreams you step into, and whatever the shop is stocking give the island its daily loop. The humor comes from Miis misreading one another and from the babble they use in place of ordinary sentences. Nudging two neighbors into a romance does not stop them quarreling about something petty an hour afterward.

Nintendo shaped the island as a place you look in on. A meal settles an immediate mood, while a catchphrase and a messy interior are how one Mii starts to feel like a particular person.
monster-hunter-4-ultimate:
Gore Magala's frenzy spreads along the roads between settlements in Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate, the Capcom hunt that became the west's major handheld Monster Hunter in 2015. Mounting lets a hunter climb a monster and topple it when the struggle holds. Guild quests, rolled with odd conditions of their own, sit beside a caravan story that travels from one village to another.

Capcom made the weapons, the monsters, and the quests. Help on the English script came from the localization studio 8-4, which did not take over making the game. Frenzied and apex states change how aggressive a familiar species feels on ground you already know.

Long weapon animations commit you, so a clean mount is often the opening that creates a safe punish. Gathering, cooking, and armor skills fill the camp before the next departure. Reading footprints and picking a weapon matchup remain the patient work these hunts demand.

As the caravan moves, the cooks, guild staff, and companions nearby change with it. Clearing an urgent monster in one hub usually opens the next stretch of that journey.
warioware-gold:
Earlier microgames and brand-new ones share a voiced story mode in WarioWare Gold, the Intelligent Systems collection Nintendo released in 2018. Wario and the regular crew introduce toys that last only a few seconds each. It arrived late in the hardware's life, among the last large Nintendo releases for that system.

A stage gives one verb, such as dodge, charge, or match a pose, and then the timer expires. A miss is immediate, and the next gag starts almost at once. Speed climbs from readable introductions into rounds that leave no time to think the prompt through.

Bosses inside the story obey the same split-second rules as the toys around them. Spoken lines fill scenes that older entries often left as text and grunts. Touch-screen gags sit beside button gags drawn from earlier volumes of the series.

Nintendo published the Intelligent Systems compilation, voice tracks included. The story gives the pile a beginning and an end, and a single toy can still be replayed for a stricter score once that plot is finished.
shin-megami-tensei-iv-apocalypse:
Nanashi walks the ruined streets in Shin Megami Tensei IV: Apocalypse, the Atlus side story released in 2016. Human partners join the party and pull the tone toward personal bonds, louder than the stern journey this plot overlaps. The events sit during Shin Megami Tensei IV, and the campaign is its own story rather than a remake.

Demon negotiation, fusion, and press-turn battles carry the fights. Factions already active in that Tokyo try to claim Nanashi, and alignment choices push back. Underground districts and surface ruins hide encounters that can end a run when the party is careless.

Bonds with those partners change scenes and some resolutions, so brushing the group off is a real decision. Resistances and skill sets still decide whether a boss pattern can be broken. Hunter associations and divine powers remain the political weather over the city.

Atlus built the midquel with ending routes of its own. A player who already knows the other protagonist will recognize places from a second angle, while someone new still meets Nanashi from the first scene.
monster-hunter-3-ultimate:
Underwater fights against Lagiacrus define Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate, Capcom's expanded village-and-port hunt on the handheld. Moga's beaches send the early quests, and Port Tanzia opens once the contracts grow larger. The release meant here is that handheld edition, separate from the Wii game Monster Hunter Tri.

Swimming shortens weapon strings and makes height part of every swing. The limiter is the awkward reach of each weapon in the water, more than a simple breath meter. Desert, forest, and volcano maps remain for hunters who want stone under their boots.

Armor skills, trap parts, and meal buffs are prepared in the village or at the port before leaving. The two hubs keep different shops and different request lists. Capturing a creature is still an alternative to carving it where it fell.

Capcom carried this generation's sea-serpent ecology onto the handheld, along with local groups for hunters who wanted company. The pace is still one quest at a time, with a loadout standing between you and the target.
paper-mario-sticker-star:
A peeled sticker might open a path or become the only command on offer in Paper Mario: Sticker Star, the Intelligent Systems journey Nintendo published in 2012. No battle partner stays in the party for the whole trip. The lands are paper craft, full of tabs, folds, and objects lifted off the scenery.

Battle stickers work as inventory. A jump, a hammer, or a fire flower is a scrap placed on a turn, and using it spends the scrap until another is found or bought. An empty album turns a short line of Goombas into a scramble.

Field stickers solve set pieces, such as a fan that must be stuck in place or a gap that needs one particular scrap. The Things, ordinary props with something inside them, serve as the large encounters. Desert, forest, snow, and harbor kingdoms are built from those crafts rather than from one town full of allies.

Intelligent Systems pointed this outing away from The Thousand-Year Door. Growth lives in the sticker album instead of a climbing experience level, and Nintendo's publishing put that album on the handheld.
professor-layton-and-the-azran-legacy:
Aurora, a living remnant of the Azran civilization, sends Hershel Layton's last prequel around the globe in Professor Layton and the Azran Legacy, from Level-5 and Nintendo in 2013. The case closes that trilogy of prequels. Curious Village is a different, earlier introduction, and this one does not present him as a stranger to riddles.

Ice fields, jungle ruins, and buried sites each stop the party at a gate made of a riddle. Luke and Emmy travel with Aurora while rival searchers try to seize what the Azran left behind. The stylus writes answers, rotates devices, and marks the single spot a diagram demands.

The script keeps treating the journey as a farewell. Careful reading does more work than reflex. A bad assumption about a picture can spend hint coins even when the counting itself looks easy.

Level-5 constructed the Azran plot as the capstone, and Nintendo published that handheld edition. Every ruin chosen on the world map adds a piece of what the civilization built, and the finish has to settle Aurora's purpose together with the chase.
professor-layton-and-the-miracle-mask:
A mask that grants miracles draws young Hershel and Randall through the carnival city of Monte d'Or in Professor Layton and the Miracle Mask, the Level-5 prequel Nintendo published in 2012. Riddles appear as solid dioramas the stylus can turn and poke. The case is set before the gentleman detective's later fame, back when the two of them were students of ruins and tricks.

Hint coins let a stuck player move on, though the story would rather have an answer. Block slides, drawn routes, and questions about crowds fit a city obsessed with wonders. The miracles look impossible until the investigation catches the mask up.

Randall's ambition and Hershel's caution put the strain into the flashbacks. A later walk down the same streets ties the boys' expedition to the disasters hitting Monte d'Or now. Extra riddles hide in corners for anyone who wants more than the critical path.

Level-5 built the case and Nintendo published the handheld edition. Voiced scenes frame a mystery about what the two friends owed each other, and finishing it means answering both the street wonders and the older dig that uncovered the artifact.
fantasy-life:
The same hero can stand as a paladin and later as a cook or a miner in Fantasy Life, the Level-5 tale Nintendo released in 2014, with the butterfly Flutter pulling the story along. Ore from a mining shift can become the blade carried on the road, because crafting and combat belong to one character. Lives are jobs you switch between, not separate save files.

Each Life keeps its own ranks, trials, and master. A miner looks for nodes out in the field, a cook works ingredients at a station, and a paladin takes the monsters blocking a road. Gear earned in a crafting Life feeds the Lives that do the fighting.

Flutter's request is the excuse to visit new regions. Towns hold the shops and the masters who set the next license test. Staying off the main path for a long stretch still uses the game as it was built, because those jobs are the body of it.

Level-5 developed the job systems, and Nintendo published them. The mood stays gentle even when a larger monster guards a later region, and learning several Lives is how the hero grows capable.
kingdom-hearts-3d-dream-drop-distance:
A Drop gauge swaps who you guide between Sora and Riku in Kingdom Hearts 3D: Dream Drop Distance, the Square Enix exam set in sleeping worlds in 2012. The pair are sitting the Mark of Mastery. Dream Eaters serve as allies and as enemies, and Flowmotion turns wall runs and swings into the way fights travel.

When the gauge empties, the boy in your hands falls asleep and the other wakes on a route of his own. Portals join familiar worlds that have slipped into sleep. Abilities live on a command deck triggered in real time.

Flowmotion can bridge a gap or stretch a combo, and it can also fling the character off a ledge if the move is held too long. Dream Eaters can be created, fed, and brought along with skills of their own. Judges of the exam, and figures waiting inside the dreams, push events past a sightseeing tour of those worlds.

Square Enix is the studio credited with the exam. Finishing it means keeping both boys alive on their separate routes until the story locks them back together.
rhythm-heaven-megamix:
Tibby, fallen out of Heaven World, gives the remixes a reason to exist in Rhythm Heaven Megamix, Nintendo's 2016 tower of rhythm games old and new. Floors hold stages from across the series, plus new ones built for this collection. You answer with buttons or with the stylus, according to the cue and the control setting.

A perfect hit occupies a narrow window, and a slightly late tap is still a miss you can hear. Some games are one repeated flick, while others change tempo halfway down the track. The tower map shows which floor is open and which remix is still shut.

Helping Tibby climb toward home unlocks the next bundle of stages, and that story is what ties the remixes together. A remix stitches several games into one longer piece, the point where the earlier floors are tested. One stage can be tried again for a higher rating without climbing the entire tower.

Nintendo assembled the anthology on the handheld. Harder versions of the games remain after the story, aimed at players who want a less forgiving beat.
metal-gear-solid-snake-eater-3d:
Crouch walking and photo camouflage were added when Kojima Productions and Konami placed the jungle mission on the handheld as Metal Gear Solid Snake Eater 3D in 2012. The lower screen keeps the map and the camouflage readout. The operation in that jungle is the same mission the earlier game told, rather than a plot written fresh for this hardware.

Snake still crawls, climbs trees, and swaps uniforms so a patrol looks past him. Point a camera at a surface and the picture can become a camouflage pattern. Close punches and the tranq pistol remain the quiet ways through a guard line.

Food that spoils, a cure list, and the stamina bar all survive the move onto two screens. Boss encounters still want a particular approach, whether that means outlasting a sniper or living through a chase on the water. Gear is checked on the touch screen so the view above stays clear.

Kojima Productions developed the mission, and Konami published this version of it. An alert still brings more soldiers, so a blown disguise costs more than one bar of health.
donkey-kong-country-returns-3d:
An extra cloud world waits past the mine-cart lines in Donkey Kong Country Returns 3D, the stereoscopic port Nintendo published in 2013. The Wii game underneath is Retro Studios' work. Rocket barrels and the demand to hold a run through spikes remain, and the Super Nintendo Country is a different set of levels.

Donkey Kong slams the ground, rolls, and puffs a breath of air to uncover bananas. Once Diddy is found he rides on Kong's back and grants a short hover. A lot of worlds close on a cart or a barrel run that punishes any hesitation.

Cloud platforms are the plainest addition on this cartridge. Depth shows most in the foreground props and in the long drops. A pit during a cart ride offers no gentle landing, which is why balloons and spare lives matter on those rails.

Nintendo published the handheld edition, Retro Studios' stages plus that added world. Hidden pieces and the K-O-N-G letters still sit off the obvious path for anyone chasing a complete set.
yo-kai-watch:
A wristwatch that reveals invisible spirits is the whole invitation of Yo-kai Watch, Level-5's 2013 phenomenon built around Whisper and Jibanyan. You befriend yo-kai, then rotate a wheel of them during battle instead of choosing from a fixed list. The game was a huge hit in Japan and later reached players in the west on the handheld.

Whisper fills the role of a fussy butler who explains each haunting. Jibanyan is a cat spirit with a very narrow set of obsessions, and he is usually among the first fighters placed on the wheel. Everyday streets hide the spirits causing small troubles, and the lens makes them visible enough to talk to, feed, or fight.

Stopping the wheel on the right beat lines up a Soultimate technique. Food, mood, and luck decide whether a defeated spirit agrees to come along, so the same one may refuse a second time. Fresh districts, and a spirit world past them, open as the requests accumulate.

Level-5 designed the watch, the roster of medals, and the light daily errands. The loop is to wander, befriend, and spin that wheel, settling whatever has been bothering the people on the street.
shin-megami-tensei-devil-survivor-overcl:
Spoken scenes and a new eighth day were added in Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Survivor Overclocked, Atlus's 2011 remake of the tactics lockdown. A death clock on the COMP still counts toward the moment Tokyo's barrier finishes anyone left inside. The original Devil Survivor release on the earlier handheld is a separate game.

Human leaders and the demon teams under them fight on a grid. When a leader falls, that squad's contribution collapses with them. Between the story's clocks, fusion and skill cracking are how the group grows strong enough for the next timed crisis.

The eighth day runs past conclusions the first version did not contain. Lines you choose steer who lives through the lockdown. Cracking a skill off an enemy leader and fusing it onto your own team is the slow growth between those deadlines.

Atlus rebuilt the campaign and put voices on the major scenes. Tokyo's map works as a schedule: miss a place before the clock jumps and that event is gone.
detective-pikachu:
A Pikachu who talks and drinks coffee partners with Tim Goodman in Detective Pikachu, the Creatures case file Nintendo published in 2016. The work happens in Ryme City, where people and Pokémon share a more urban life than a trainer's road. What you are holding is that handheld mystery, and the later film does not stand in for the cases.

Scenes are walked, witnesses are questioned, and Pikachu's senses cover clues Tim cannot see. Raising the right topic opens the next lead. The partner is gruff, fond of coffee, and often a step ahead of his human.

Each district of Ryme City hosts a problem tied to a different Pokémon. Getting ahead means explaining the case, not collecting a badge from a gym. A notebook of clues keeps the interviews from turning into one long corridor.

Creatures developed the city and the partnership, and Nintendo published the cartridge. A chapter closes when the right conclusion is presented, while Tim's missing father keeps drawing the separate cases into one line.
mario-luigi-paper-jam:
Paper Toads are waiting to be rescued after a flat hero drops into the brothers' world in Mario & Luigi: Paper Jam, the AlphaDream crossover Nintendo released in 2016. Fights are trios: Mario, Luigi, and Paper Mario each take a turn under timed-hit rules. Sticker Star is a different paper outing, and Bowser's Inside Story is a different brothers game.

Out on the field, the paper hero folds into a shape the brothers can throw or ride across a gap. Waves of enemies telegraph a stomp, a hammer, or a dodge, and a missed press spoils the blow. Rounding up the scattered Toads runs through the areas as more than a motive mentioned in a cutscene.

Paired specials return as short button games, and some of them pull the third fighter in. Copy foes and papercraft set pieces put flat layers against the rounded brothers. A meeting between Bowser and a paper double supplies a large share of the jokes.

AlphaDream developed the crossover, and Nintendo published it. The journey is over only after the rescue thread and the trio battles have both been carried through.
yoshis-new-island:
A flutter jump, and stretches where Yoshi turns into a vehicle, define Yoshi's New Island, the sequel Arzest developed and Nintendo published in 2014. Baby Mario still has to be carried along, yet the island and the search for Baby Luigi are their own delivery, echoing the first trip without repeating it. Swallowed enemies become eggs to throw, and some of those eggs swell large enough to smash a wall an ordinary toss cannot break.

The flutter catches a jump that was a little late, which softens a pit next to a stricter jumping game. Helicopter, mine-cart, and submarine forms briefly replace walking with a tilt-controlled ride. Coins tucked off the main path invite a slower second visit after an exit is already known.

Big bosses absorb several volleys of eggs before they drop. A hit knocks Baby Mario off Yoshi's back and starts a countdown to catch him. Dropping into a pit skips that grace and spends a life at once.

Arzest made the sequel and Nintendo published the cartridge. Worlds still climb toward a fort and a castle, while the stork's interrupted flight keeps marking this island as a new one.
shin-megami-tensei-strange-journey-redux:
Alex, and new endings gathered around the Womb of Grief, reshape the expedition in Shin Megami Tensei: Strange Journey Redux, the remake Atlus made with Lancarse in 2018. The Schwarzwelt, the dungeon that swallowed a whole region, is still the place you crawl. The original Strange Journey on the earlier handheld remains its own release.

Battles are first-person and resolved in turns, with demons fused out of a growing compendium. Law, chaos, and a neutral reading of the disaster keep tugging the crew apart. The Womb of Grief is a dungeon added in this version, and walking it changes which conclusions can be reached.

Alex moves through the plot as a person the first expedition never met, and her presence is tied to those new endings. Gun commands share a list with demon skills, so the human crew is not helpless against whoever lives in the Schwarzwelt. Sector maps, each with its own environment, account for half of the forward progress.

Atlus and Lancarse share the credit for building the remake. An ending arrives only after the investigation has gone far enough for the alignment choices and the Womb of Grief to count.
xenoblade-chronicles-3d:
Shulk carries the Monado through a war between titans in Xenoblade Chronicles 3D, the port Monolith Soft and Nintendo released for the New Nintendo 3DS in 2015. The Bionis and the Mechonis are the colossal bodies the regions rest on. Some features are scaled back beside the Wii original, the colony story is the same one, and Xenoblade 2 is a later saga.

Arts cool on a bar during fights that run in real time, standing in the right place grants a bonus, and three characters form the active party. Visions warn Shulk that a lethal blow is coming while there is still time to answer it. Chain attacks and the Monado's arts break a Mechon's guard or topple something larger.

Only the newer model of that handheld runs the port. The fields stay enormous, and reaching a landmark opens a fast route back to it. Requests from people in the colonies sit beside the march toward the other titan.

Monolith Soft developed the campaign and Nintendo published the port. The plot still follows Shulk from the attack on Colony 9 into the question of what the sword is actually for.
mario-luigi-superstar-saga-bowsers-minio:
The Beanbean Kingdom stays in place beside a new troop-command tale in Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga + Bowser's Minions, the AlphaDream remake Nintendo published in 2017. The main book rebuilds the earlier Superstar Saga for the handheld. The added side story lets you give orders to soldiers you have recruited.

Mario and Luigi still share timed jumps and hammer strikes, both on the map and in a fight. Special moves are short input games tucked inside the turn, and a sloppy press weakens them. A stolen voice and a wandering villain remain the spine of the Beanbean plot.

Captain Goomba and the rest of the troops take a grid you direct, closer to issuing orders than to performing the button prompts yourself. Enemies you defeat can be folded into the squad. That mode runs next to the brothers' chapters instead of erasing them.

AlphaDream handled the remake and Nintendo published the package. Anyone who only wants the Beanbean journey can stay on it, while the troop missions sit there as a second campaign.
ever-oasis:
Seedlings join up while an oasis grows shop by shop in Ever Oasis, the 2017 action role-playing game Grezzo made for Nintendo with producer Koichi Ishii. Ruins wait in the desert past the water you are raising. Grezzo built it late for that hardware, out of the circle around the Mana series producer.

Residents you bring home open stalls, and those stalls supply gardens, gear, and reasons to come back between ruins. Seedlings of several races carry traversal tricks a sealed room may require. The lead fights in real time with whichever weapon was chosen for the trip.

Water, happiness, and the spread of shops change how lively the settlement feels. A ruin tends to end on a boss that wants the seedlings' skills as much as raw hits. Leaving a room unfinished often means a resident, or the stall they would have run, is still missing at home.

Ishii produced the project, Grezzo developed it, and Nintendo published it. Raising the settlement and pushing farther across the sand are a single aim, since each new resident makes the next ruin easier to clear.
pokemon-super-mystery-dungeon:
Two Pokémon wake without a clear past at the opening of Pokémon Super Mystery Dungeon, the Spike Chunsoft journey Nintendo released in 2015. A Connection Orb later calls in a huge roster drawn from across the series. Identity, and a threat aimed at Pokémon as a whole, drive the plot well past a simple errand to find one missing friend.

Floors are winding grids where items and rooms full of enemies make a straight line unlikely. Moves placed on the buttons have to cover the types ahead, or a ghostly foe becomes a wall you cannot answer. The partner stays in those corridors, and the talking keeps the lost memory from playing as an empty excuse.

Famous allies arrive through the Connection Orb once the story's conditions are met, so the team can grow far past the starting pair. A town between the corridors is where jobs are accepted and supplies are set down. Later chapters widen the danger and start asking who the pair were before they woke up.

Spike Chunsoft built the dungeon rules, and Nintendo published the handheld game. A team that falls is sent back with a penalty, and the finish comes only after that question of identity has been faced.
monster-hunter-stories:
A Kinship Stone lets a rider hatch monsters and battle beside them in Monster Hunter Stories, Capcom's turn-based rider game, with Nintendo publishing it in some regions in 2017. Navirou, a talkative Felyne, tags along as guide and comic voice. The main-series hunts, built around bringing a beast down with a greatsword, are a different sport.

Eggs discovered in dens hatch into monsties you can ride over the field and into a fight. Power, speed, and technical strikes form a three-way pattern, and winning that pattern fills kinship toward a shared skill. The ride serves as travel and as the way some encounters start.

Villages, dens, and a plot about people who partner with monsters take the place of the old quest board. Navirou talks almost without stopping, a mascot the main hunts never leaned on this heavily. The rider's weapon still counts, but a monstie's element and genes settle many of the harder matches.

Capcom developed the rider rules. Getting ahead means growing the stable and walking the story's trails, rather than clearing a timed arena against one flagship beast.
theatrhythm-final-fantasy:
Stylus notes cross field scenes, battle scenes, and event scenes in THEATRHYTHM FINAL FANTASY, the rhythm game indieszero and Square Enix released in 2012. Characters from across the series stand together as a party. Numbered Final Fantasy quests, with their towns and world maps, are a different kind of game.

Battle stages throw enemies in with the notes, and a missed tap spends both the chain and hit points. Field stages are plainer walks along a road of beats. Event stages play back a remembered scene while the stylus keeps the melody's time.

Skills belonging to the party you assembled can fire in the middle of a song. Crystals, and a lengthening list of tunes, are the goals that last. A perfect chain feels nothing like a stage you barely survived, and the result screen says which of the two you earned.

indieszero built the touch-screen sessions together with Square Enix. Flicks, holds, and taps meet the icons sliding toward a line, and finishing a song pushes the collection forward.
radiant-historia-perfect-chronology:
Stocke keeps two histories of one war in Radiant Historia: Perfect Chronology, the Atlus expansion of his time-travel quest. Crossing between those records still changes who survives a battle. Added episodes hang on the branches, with room for characters beyond the party that first traveled with him. Players received the lengthened chronicle in 2018.

Columns of enemies turn positioning into the point of a fight. A shove, a trap, or a delayed blow can slam one foe into the next. Choosing when Stocke revisits a decision node matters as much as the sword swing.

Sealed events open only after an earlier choice is rewritten, so the map is cause and effect rather than a straight road. One record follows the military crisis. Its twin follows a different chain of sacrifices, and the two answer each other.

Anyone looking for the Nintendo DS original will find a shorter, separate chronicle. Extra episodes and space for further characters are what the remake adds to Stocke's histories. Atlus rebuilt that expanded time travel for the later handheld.
bravely-second-end-layer:
Yew Geneolgia faces a moon that has become the threat in Bravely Second: End Layer, Square Enix's sequel to the prior job-and-turn adventure. Magnolia comes down from that moon carrying warnings the surface does not have. Outside Japan, Nintendo published the sequel that arrived in 2016.

Saving a turn still braces a fighter and banks the action, while spending the stock unleashes a chain. New jobs change which abilities can ride that gamble. Asterisk holders interrupt the road, each with a doctrine and a combat kit of their own.

Army ties make the lunar approach personal for Yew. His losses, paired with Magnolia's knowledge of the moon, push the plot past a simple villain chase. Leadership sits with those two, rather than with the heroes who closed the previous story.

Bravely Default remains the earlier calamity, with its own protagonists. Brave and Default stay at the center of combat here, both aimed at the moon. Square Enix made the sequel, and Nintendo handled publication beyond Japan.
rune-factory-4:
Selphia wakes a royal amnesiac in Rune Factory 4, and the farmer you guide is either a prince or a princess who remembers neither crown. Neverland built the blend of fields, fights, and courtship. XSEED and Marvelous brought that life west in 2013.

Orders arrive from Ventuswill, the dragon who watches the capital. Between her commands you till soil, battle monsters past the town edge, and grow close enough to neighbors to marry them. A crop, a festival, or a villager's request can outweigh the next dungeon.

Earlier entries on the DS belong to other towns and other memories. Selphia, the lost title, and Ventuswill's requests frame the Nintendo 3DS entry. Companions raised on the farm can follow you into a fight, linking the barn to the battlefield.

Chores never fully step aside for the royal mystery. Townsfolk address the stranger as royalty while the streets are still unfamiliar. Neverland's harvest-and-hunt calendar, carried west by XSEED and Marvelous, is how Selphia is lived.
star-wars-rogue-squadron-ii-rogue-leader:
Factor 5 and LucasArts opened the GameCube era with Star Wars Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader, putting Luke Skywalker in a cockpit from the Battle of Naboo through Endor. Medal targets grade each sortie past simply surviving it. Players saw that launch showcase in 2001.

Naboo's starfighters, the snow at Hoth, and the Death Star approach each demand a different hand on the throttle. Stray shots, a protected wingman, or a clock barely met can decide the medal. Replaying a film battle for a sharper debrief is how a mission stays alive after the first clear.

Luke is the pilot named on the box, while Rebel craft and their wingmen fill out the squadron. Dense fighter swarms and long trench runs were there to show what the new hardware could draw. Flight modeling was Factor 5's job, and LucasArts shared the production.

An earlier Nintendo 64 campaign already used the Rogue Squadron name and a different mission list. Naboo-to-Endor sorties in that launch window are what the subtitle names. Medal hunting is written into the debrief rather than glued on afterward.
persona-q2-new-cinema-labyrinth:
A movie house locks its doors on three casts at once in Persona Q2: New Cinema Labyrinth, Atlus's dungeon where Persona 3, Persona 4, and Persona 5 share one theater. Hikari is bound to that screen, and she is why the exits fail. Atlus shipped the handheld labyrinth in 2018.

Floors are dressed as films that have to finish before the next reel. Mapping the corridors still matters, and elemental weaknesses still swing a random fight, yet the walls look like sets. Allies who never shared a school calendar argue through the same projection.

Hikari's bond with the cinema is the mystery, and she belongs to this labyrinth rather than arriving as a guest from one numbered team. Phantom Thieves, the Investigation Team, and SEES compare notes under a single projector. Her relationship to the reels is why the doors closed.

Persona Q crossed two casts inside another labyrinth. Thieves from the fifth game join here, and the movie house replaces that earlier premise. It was the last Persona game released on the handheld.
donkey-konga:
Namco turned a pair of bongos into the controller for Donkey Konga, a rhythm session Nintendo published, scored by hits, claps, and deliberate rests. Donkey Kong and Diddy Kong host while the track plays. Classic melodies share the list with licensed songs, and the drum party arrived in 2003.

Striking the drumhead answers a hit cue. Clapping to the side answers a different cue. During a rest both hands stay quiet, and playing through that silence counts as a miss.

Barrel hops and mine-cart chases are somebody else's challenge. Here DK and Diddy are hosts, not athletes clearing a stage. Keeping time with the playlist they introduce is the whole test.

Hit, clap, and pause were the three responses Namco built the sessions around. Publication of that living-room music game fell to Nintendo. Licensed recordings sit beside tunes already associated with the ape and his smaller partner.
wario-world:
Treasure's only Wario platform brawler is Wario World, a three-dimensional beat-em-up Nintendo published, where punches, piledrivers, and garlic free trapped sprites. Shoulder throws and slams clear the arenas. Treasure and Nintendo released that fist-first quest in 2004.

Dashing into a punch opens the bullying, and the piledriver finishes a grabbed foe. Coins feed Wario's greed, yet the sprites caged inside a level are the real errand. Cloves picked up along the way pay the cost of opening those cages.

Leave the garlic behind and the prisoners stay shut, so the food and the wrestling share one route. Jumps exist, but grabs and body slams cover the ground between cages. Brawling arenas, not puzzle rooms, are how those spaces were built.

WarioWare breaks attention into microgames that vanish in a moment. Weight, grabs, and a continuous arena keep the quest a brawl. No later brawler from the studio repeated this kind of Wario fight.
pokemon-channel:
Sofa time with Pikachu is the loop of Pokémon Channel, the GameCube companionship piece Ambrella made and Nintendo published, in which changing channels replaces trainer battles. A quiz show and Meowth slowly thread the broadcasts into a story. Ambrella's unhurried schedule belongs to 2003.

Shopping spots, creature features, and odd short programs rotate as the hours pass. Pikachu reacts on the cushion beside you instead of waiting in a battle lineup. Picking what airs next is how the afternoon moves.

Meowth's scheme around the quiz program gives those idle hours a plot to check. Everything in the apartment is arranged around the television. Gym badges and capture tallies never enter that room.

Ambrella framed the console piece as shared viewing rather than a trainer campaign. That quieter design carries a Nintendo publishing credit. What tension exists stays with a broadcast and a scheming Meowth.
dragon-quest-vii-fragments-of-the-forgot:
Lost islands rise when fragments return to the tablet in Dragon Quest VII: Fragments of the Forgotten Past, the remake ArtePiazza and Square Enix built from the PlayStation saga. Compared with that PlayStation version, the script runs shorter and the cast is modeled in three dimensions. English players received the Nintendo 3DS edition, published by Nintendo, in 2016.

From Estard the party sails toward shores the sea had erased. Each restored land brings a trouble of its own, then another fragment opens the next gap. Job classes branch across those recovered regions. Reassembling the broken map is the campaign's spine.

Scenes that sprawled across the original PlayStation release move faster after the trim. Class changes and the island quest both survive that cut. Dimensional heroes stand in for the older field sprites of the first disc.

Dragon Quest VIII follows a cursed king on another continent and does not use this tablet. ArtePiazza and Square Enix made the remake together. Repairing the horizon one fragment at a time is the English edition Nintendo published for the Nintendo 3DS.
inazuma-eleven:
Mark Evans, Endou in the Japanese script, captains Inazuma Eleven, Level-5's soccer story in which special shots exist only after the plot teaches them. Western players on the Nintendo 3DS met his team in 2014, after the series had already started on the DS in Japan, so both handhelds belong in the telling.

Conversation is what unlocks a kick, a block, or a goalkeeper feat before the whistle blows. Friendship and training numbers sit underneath the footwork. Two halves turn the match into a long encounter, and a gauge is spent on those story-taught shots.

Raimon is the school side under Mark's captaincy, and the same boy is Endou when the names stay Japanese. Japan met the tale on the DS before anyone abroad did. Abroad, the adventure arrived on the 3DS, so the two machines can be named together.

Level-5 treats the spectacular kick as something the narrative has to unlock. Until that scene happens, the shot is not yours to call. Binding a story technique to a live match is the identity of this soccer tale.
code-of-princess:
Solange Blanchefleur De Lux fights with a very long sword in Code of Princess, a side-view brawler of combos and a fantasy cast. Studio Saizensen developed the battles. Western players got the Nintendo 3DS release from Atlus in 2012.

Attack strings launch and juggle whoever stands ahead of her. Blade reach decides the spacing, so a shorter ally solves the same scrolling lane another way. Other fighters carry their own weapons and temperaments into those side-on brawls.

Her full noble name sits inside the kingdom's crisis, not on a throwaway caption. Stages scroll as fights rather than as maps searched for keys. Knowing which hit leads into the next outweighs sorting a pack of spells.

Combo routes are Studio Saizensen's work. Outside Japan, the release belonged to Atlus. An extended sword, a sideways camera, and an ensemble of fantasy fighters make up the offer.
harvest-moon-magical-melody:
Musical notes scattered through town are the restoration project of Harvest Moon: Magical Melody, the Marvelous GameCube farm where the collection brings the place back. Either a boy or a girl can head the household. Jamie is bound to that note list, and the console release is from 2005.

Crops, animals, and favors for neighbors continue while the notes are hunted. Every note brought back is a step toward hearing music in the streets again. The checklist, not a lifetime divided into chapters, decides when the town is whole.

A Wonderful Life, on the same console, follows a family's seasons in a valley and never centers this musical errand. Choosing a boy or a girl changes who walks these streets, and the list still waits either way. Jamie keeps the search personal.

Marvelous built the days from ordinary chores plus a score you assemble by hand. Find the notes and the town revives. The valley-and-family tale does not ask you to finish Jamie's list.
baten-kaitos-eternal-wings-and-the-lost-:
Magnus cards act as weapons, photographs, and items across the floating islands of Baten Kaitos: Eternal Wings and the Lost Ocean. Kalas travels with a guardian spirit the player inhabits. Monolith Soft and tri-Crescendo developed the journey, Namco published it, and Yasunori Mitsuda wrote the score that reached listeners in 2003.

Fights are hands built from that deck. Fruit can age into another effect, a photograph can strike, and a sword is only one more card played on the right beat. Islands suspended in open sky turn every road into a voyage among broken continents.

Kalas's own wing and his exchanges with the guardian spirit keep the plot between the two of them. The spirit is addressed as a companion rather than ignored as a cursor. Mitsuda's music carries that sky-and-ocean air from one drifting land to the next.

Baten Kaitos Origins tells a later story and is not this introduction. Deck, winged lead, spirit, and floating lands were established together in this journey. Monolith Soft, tri-Crescendo, and Namco share that first production.
mario-golf-toadstool-tour:
Chosen side-spin and shots unique to each golfer define Mario Golf: Toadstool Tour, Camelot's GameCube round published by Nintendo. Fairways cut through the Mushroom Kingdom, and a club set is packed before the first tee. Camelot and Nintendo issued the tour in 2003.

Calling a draw or a fade is an input, not merely a miss. Club, green break, and that golfer's special shape stack into one stroke. Mario's line and Peach's line on the same hole are different tools.

Anonymous resort scenery is gone. Grounds beside Peach's castle, Bowser's badlands, and other kingdom landmarks are the holes themselves. Learning one roster member's specialty can clear a carry another body will not reach.

Separate from this round, the Game Boy Advance Mario Golf is its own handheld game. Camelot's spin, the per-character shot table, and those club sets on kingdom courses belong here. Publishing credit for the console tour sits with Nintendo.
monster-hunter-generations:
Four Hunting Styles reshape a weapon in Monster Hunter Generations, Capcom's hunt built on Guild, Striker, Aerial, and Adept together with Hunter Arts. Prowler mode sends you out as a Palico instead of a human hunter. Deviant monsters, Hellblade Glavenus among them, stand apart from ordinary quarry. Capcom released the installment in 2016.

Whichever style is equipped rewrites dodges and combo paths before the monster is even sighted. Aerial hunters treat leaving the ground as footwork. Adept hunters convert a timed evade into an opening, Striker leans on arts, and Guild keeps a broader traditional kit.

Under Prowler rules a Palico has a separate skill list and a smaller frame in the same locale. That cat hunts alone instead of trailing a human partner. Hunter Arts fill a gauge and then spend according to the style that was chosen.

Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate does not put this four-way style split at its center. Deviant quarries, the styles, and the Prowler option arrive together on the Nintendo 3DS. Picking Aerial or Adept as a human, or going out as a Palico, is the choice waiting before the quest.
star-wars-rogue-squadron-iii-rebel-strik:
On-foot missions join the sorties in Star Wars Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike, Factor 5's extension of the flight formula. Wedge Antilles and other pilots share the campaign with those ground stretches. When the Rogue Leader disc is on hand a second player can join, and the mixed tour arrived in 2003.

Sabotage, speeder runs, and firefights ask for boots where a pure cockpit game would stay airborne. Afterward the view returns to a ship for bombing passes and dogfights. Handoffs between ground and cockpit are what the third installment is built around.

Wedge leads assignments rather than commenting from the edge of a single-hero radio drama. Several pilots divide the work, so the Rebel job spreads across the squadron. Cooperative seats depend on the earlier disc, and without it the campaign stays solo.

Rogue Leader itself remains a separate flight game. Infantry objectives and the disc-linked partner belong only to this chapter. Factor 5 made stepping out of the cockpit part of the work.
super-monkey-ball-2:
Dr. Bad-Boon's plot frames the mazes of Super Monkey Ball 2, the Amusement Vision sequel Sega published. AiAi still rolls inside a ball, the story courses run harder, and the party-game list outgrows the first Monkey Ball. Sega released the follow-up in 2002.

Tilting shifts the floor, and the monkey inside the sphere can only obey gravity. Corners become questions of slope and speed. Story stages abandon the gentle introductory ramps in a hurry.

Cutscenes cast Bad-Boon as the troublemaker who arranged this new gauntlet. Rolling physics then fill a larger group of mini-games than the earlier ball game carried. Bananas, narrow rails, and sudden gaps remain the course language.

Amusement Vision built the harder mazes and the wider party menu. Sega published the sequel that contains them. AiAi's ball and Bad-Boon's scheme arrive together.
warioware-inc-mega-party-games:
Up to four people take the couch for WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Party Games!, Nintendo's GameCube party version of the microgame collection. One action answers a flashing prompt, and a different absurd task replaces it within seconds. Four-player couch play shipped from Nintendo in 2004.

Solo play lives on the Game Boy Advance cartridge, while Twisted is a separate motion-controlled entry. Neither one is this four-player shell. Tiny challenges sit inside modes a single handheld screen was never asked to host.

Each microgame still lasts only a breath. Surviving the instruction matters more than mastering a system. Board-like contests string those bursts into an argument over who flinched.

Wario's fictional firm, named in the logo, is the host of the console party. Shared structure around those sudden jobs is what the disc adds. Neither the handheld original nor Twisted matches this party shell.
1080deg-avalanche:
Escape routes fail behind the rider in 1080° Avalanche, Nintendo's sequel to 1080 Snowboarding, pairing trick courses with descents where the snow itself is the timer. Hesitation on an avalanche run lets the wave catch the board. GameCube received that follow-up from Nintendo in 2003.

Trick stages still demand spins, rails, and clean landings. Escape stages turn that same feel for speed and recovery into a flight from the collapse. Both trust one snowboarder to decide when to commit.

Competitive downhill, not a collapsing slope, was the aim of the earlier snowboarding game. Trick vocabulary stays, and survival descents are the new half. Development of that combination stayed inside Nintendo.

Scored exhibitions occupy some of the mountains. Other runs are lost the moment the avalanche touches a tail edge. Exhibition set beside escape is how the sequel is divided.
metal-arms-glitch-in-the-system:
Glitch bolts a lost arm back into place before the jokes and the gunfire of Metal Arms: Glitch in the System, the third-person shooter Mass Media made and Vivendi published. General Corrosive commands the robot army opposite him. Other consoles received editions, yet the release described here is the GameCube one from 2003.

Scrap, firearms, and a rebuilt shoulder carry a comic war through factories and battlefields. Humor stays loud while the shots stay lethal. One small robot climbs Corrosive's chain of command.

Mass Media gave Glitch both the voice and the shooting. Vivendi put the campaign out. Machines staff the rooms, and the targets can talk while they fall.

Same bolted arm and the same general both belong to the GameCube release. Versions on other hardware do not replace that edition. Jokes and robot targets keep the war comic.
viewtiful-joe-2:
Silvia fights as a second lead beside Joe in Viewtiful Joe 2, the Clover Studio sequel Capcom published. Slow, zoom, and mach speed are the VFX powers that turn each brawl into a directed shot. Both heroes carry the film-within-a-game structure forward, and the sequel arrived in 2004.

Holding time open lets a dodge mature into a counter. Zoom swells a hit until it crowds the frame. Mach speed turns a sprint into damage, and Silvia times that same trio with her own reach.

Sets behave like scenes from a picture that is already running. Choosing which VFX stays live matters as much as the next punch. Clover Studio keeps the movie logic and splits the lead between the pair.

Silvia stays off the playable lead pair in the first Viewtiful Joe. Capcom still publishes, and she finally shares the lead. Slow, zoom, and mach speed remain the grammar, now divided instead of kept to Joe alone.
billy-hatcher-and-the-giant-egg-2003:
Billy rolls a giant egg through Morning Land in Billy Hatcher and the Giant Egg (2003), hatching helpers and fighting the crows that overrun the morning world. Sonic Team's platformer, published by Sega, never hands the stages to Sonic. Pushing the shell until it breaks, the chicken-cap hero frees a helper.

Steering a small shell is a puzzle, while a grown one bowls straight through the flock. Momentum supplies the hit. Whichever creature emerges then has a job in the following stretch, so the egg that was fed becomes the tool.

Crows occupy Morning Land. Nests, switches, and scattered flocks are the reasons to push the shell uphill. Sonic Team built the mascot run around that egg-roller, and Sega published the crow-fighting courses.

Breaking the shell pays out and arms the next stretch at the same moment. Hatching the fitting animal answers the obstacle ahead. Rolling, growing, and using what emerges, against those crows, is the whole action.
donkey-kong-jungle-beat:
Clapping the bongo controller throws a punch in Donkey Kong Jungle Beat, the Nintendo EAD Tokyo game where drumming makes Donkey Kong run and vines haul him across gaps. Rhythm is the movement, not a side activity. Country Returns is a different game from this athletic jungle course, released in 2004.

Beating the drums builds his sprint. A clap becomes the strike. Grabbing a vine uses the same controller that just played the beat, so a slipped rhythm turns into a missed leap.

Courses are graded like performances while he chases through the trees. Strong chains of beats share that grade with simply reaching the goal. EAD Tokyo built this ape around the instrument.

Country Returns later sent him on a sideways trek with ordinary buttons and another team. Inputs in this jungle stay percussive, from clap to dash to vine. EAD Tokyo, working as Nintendo's team, turned Kong into an athletic drum performance.
pokemon-mystery-dungeon-explorers-of-dar:
You and a chosen partner share the guild halls of Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Darkness, and the plot turns on a time traveler. Chunsoft shipped that story in 2008, with Nintendo publishing the cartridge. The hero wakes in Treasure Town as a Pokémon who used to be human, then signs on at Wigglytuff's guild.

Floors rebuild themselves on every visit, and the pair take turns under a belly clock that punishes a long stay. Wild Pokémon can join on the way back to the stairs. After the main case, special episodes open as side stories you can start from the guild.

Grovyle is bound into the time-travel thread rather than parked as a random boss. Explorers of Time is the companion version, with the same backbone and a different set of recruits. The earlier Rescue Team pair uses another guild entirely, and Explorers of Sky is a later, larger release.

Your partner talks through the journey and fights on the same turn order as the hero. A defeat on a deep floor can dump the team outside without the item they came to fetch, so supplies matter. That partnership is the spine Chunsoft wrote around the amnesia and the crisis arriving from the future.
golden-sun-dark-dawn:
Matthew, son of Isaac, leads the new adepts of Golden Sun: Dark Dawn. Camelot set their journey in 2010, thirty years after the first games, on a Weyard broken open by the last Golden Sun. Karis and Tyrell start beside him, children of adepts who walked the earlier roads.

Djinn still latch onto characters and rewrite their classes. Psynergy remains the elemental craft used in battle and on the field. The geography itself is a scar: seas and land shifted when alchemy returned, and a crisis known as the Grave Eclipse hangs over that altered map.

This sequel is neither the first Golden Sun nor The Lost Age. Those earlier stories belong to Matthew's parents. Here the next generation crosses the aftermath on its own routes, collecting Djinn the elders do not carry for them.

Nintendo published the Camelot game. The party grows past the opening trio as new adepts join. The old heroes appear as parents and elders rather than as the group you command.
pokemon-ranger-guardian-signs:
Befriending starts with a loop drawn around a wild Pokémon in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs. Creatures and Nintendo released this third Ranger adventure in 2010. The line has to stay unbroken while the creature struggles, or the capture fails.

Ranger Signs are a separate gesture. You draw a stored sign and trigger a field effect that a capture loop cannot perform. Ukulele Pichu, a small Pichu carrying an instrument, belongs to the story rather than to a random patch of grass.

The plot moves between present-day Oblivia and an earlier era of those same islands. Work done in one time changes what you can reach in the other. That split is why the job feels different from a single-era patrol.

The original Pokémon Ranger and Shadows of Almia came first, each with its own region. This entry keeps the capture stylus and adds the sign book. Both drawings share the touch screen, and they are not the same motion.
super-princess-peach:
Peach sets out to rescue Mario in Super Princess Peach, with a talking umbrella named Perry beside her. Tose built the journey and Nintendo published it in 2006. Bowser has stirred Vibe Island, and the path to Mario runs across that place.

Joy, gloom, rage, and calm are her powers. Joy helps her float, gloom brings tears that douse and strike, rage wraps her in a charge, and calm lets her recover. Each vibe also changes how Perry behaves.

The umbrella talks, swings, and answers the mood she is wearing. Stages are areas of Vibe Island rather than a tour of the Mushroom Kingdom. Mario is the one waiting to be saved, which reverses the usual chase.

Vibe energy has to be gathered if the four moods are going to stay ready. Perry can cross gaps that a normal jump will not. Tose built the cartridge around that emotion set.
trauma-center-under-the-knife:
Derek Stiles is the surgeon under your stylus in Trauma Center: Under the Knife. Atlus opened his first hospital posting in 2005. He works at Hope Hospital while nurse Angie Thompson hands him tools and calls the next crisis.

Incisions, forceps, antibiotic gel, and sutures are ordinary motions before anything unnatural appears. The Healing Touch slows the clock when a procedure starts to fail, and the slowdown cannot be held forever. A steady stylus line matters more than fast button taps.

GUILT viruses arrive as growths that ordinary surgery does not cover. Each strain asks for its own sequence of cuts, drains, and lasers. The operations teach the tools first, then demand them in combination.

Second Opinion is a later rework on Wii, not this cartridge. Atlus told Derek's first outbreak on the original handheld release. Later nights assume you already know how to suture under a shrinking timer.
cooking-mama:
A recipe in Cooking Mama is a chain of short kitchen tests, and Office Create released that first entry in 2006. You chop, stir, and plate, each step with its own gesture. Miss the timing and Mama scolds the result, then finishes the dish herself.

Chopping tracks the stylus like a knife. Stirring wants a steady circle. Plating has to drop the food on the outline she shows, and a sloppy landing brings the disappointed face.

Majesco published the cartridge in the United States. Taito published it in Japan. The two boxes lead into the same kitchen and the same judging.

Later collections added more dishes, so the menu here is the original one. There is no restaurant to manage between recipes. You cook, you hear the verdict, and you turn to the next card.
scribblenauts:
Maxwell writes a noun and the object appears, which is the trick of Scribblenauts. 5th Cell built the notebook and Warner Bros. published it in 2009. If the word names a thing, that thing drops into the level ready to push, ride, or ignite.

Each puzzle hides a Starite, and the stage rarely names the one correct object. A ladder, a rope, or something stranger can all be legitimate when the physics cooperate. The pleasure is inventing a solution the simulator still has to honor.

This first outing understands nouns and little else. Color, weight, and other describing words arrived only in the sequel, so a crate here is only a crate. You cannot paint it by typing an adjective in front of the noun.

Maxwell moves between those Starite problems with the notebook as his inventory. Spawn too many objects and the level can choke on its own clutter. Warner Bros. shipped that toy as 5th Cell designed it, nouns first.
warioware-diy:
Intelligent Systems and Nintendo turned WarioWare: D.I.Y. into a 2010 workshop where the stylus builds the microgames, music included. You draw the pictures, decide what the player must do, and record a tiny tune. A finished piece lasts only a few seconds, in keeping with Wario's usual pace.

The maker asks for graphics, sound, and a clear condition rather than handing over a prebuilt toy. A bomb, a face, or a bouncing ball can be the entire challenge. Wario still frames the collection, but the jokes are the ones you authored.

Homemade pieces can be swapped with another player. The exchange does not ask for a shop or a second copy of the workshop. You hand over the microgame you just drew and try the one you receive.

WarioWare: Touched! is a different cartridge, packed with finished microgames instead of a workshop. This release is the maker. Intelligent Systems kept the brief timing and gave the drawing and music tools to the player.
drawn-to-life:
The hero of Drawn to Life does not exist until you sketch him, and the same ink supplies his weapons and the platforms under his feet. 5th Cell built that drawing adventure and THQ published it in 2007. A blank outline becomes a body because the player fills it in.

The Raposa are the villagers who ask for that hero. Their village is the hub between sketched levels. Ink is both the medium on the page and the darkness pressing in on the town.

A weapon drawn at the start shows up in his hands during a stage. Platforms you design become the ground he crosses. A careless sketch is the hitbox and the foothold, not a sticker pasted over a finished sprite.

THQ published this original DS cartridge. A 505 Games credit belongs to other issues, not to the first release. The Raposa story here is the one 5th Cell made with THQ.
ace-attorney-investigations-2:
Miles Edgeworth investigates crimes himself in Ace Attorney Investigations 2, with Kay Faraday beside him in the field. Capcom released the DS cartridge in Japan under the name Gyakuten Kenji 2. That Japanese release, dated 2011, was not an English DS edition.

Logic chess is the new clash. You face a witness and break a chain of contradictions move by move, beside Edgeworth's older habit of connecting clues. Kay's thieving skills open paths a prosecutor would not normally walk.

No official English script shipped on the original DS cartridge for a Western launch. An official English version came years later on other platforms. Those later platforms are where that official English script lives.

Edgeworth is no longer only the rival across from a defense attorney. He walks the scene, and Kay is the partner who slips past locks. Logic chess keeps the arguments from repeating the first Investigations game beat for beat.
sonic-rush-adventure:
Sonic and Blaze share a ship off Southern Island in Sonic Rush Adventure. Dimps and Sonic Team developed the voyage, and Sega published it in 2007. Marine, a raccoon who wants a captain's chair, pulls them into the local trouble.

Sea charts link the islands, and the boost carries the craft across open water. You plot a route, then spend that meter to cover the distance. Once you make landfall, stages still run as fast side-view sprints.

Blaze travels as Sonic's equal, not as a guest for a single zone. The ship is the hub between landfalls. Southern Island is home base rather than one beach course.

The voyage is the sequel to Sonic Rush, not a chapter of Sonic Colors. Sega's credits put Dimps and Sonic Team on the same game. The charts and the water boost are the features that separate it from a plain remix of the first Rush stages.
dragon-quest-iv-chapters-of-the-chosen-2:
Square Enix rebuilt the Famicom story as Dragon Quest IV: Chapters of the Chosen, a DS remake from 2008 with Akira Toriyama's art drawn again. The chapter structure remains. Ragnar, Alena, Torneko, and the twin seers Meena and Maya each receive a chapter before the hero does.

Party chat lets you speak with companions in towns and on the road, which the older cartridge did not do. The hero's chapter still comes last, so the chosen ones gather before you guide the final member. North American players once knew the NES cartridge as Dragon Warrior IV.

Battles keep a first-person encounter view, now with redrawn monsters. A wagon and a growing lineup return once the separate tales converge. You are not handed one continuous biography from the title screen.

Toriyama's new illustrations replace the older portraits and bestiary drawings. Square Enix kept the chapter order instead of folding every hero into a single opening. The chat lines are the remake's clearest new voice.
final-fantasy-12-revenant-wings:
Vaan leads a crew of sky pirates through Ivalice in Final Fantasy XII: Revenant Wings. Square Enix and Think & Feel released that sequel in 2007. It plays in real time on DS, and it is not the PlayStation 2 game that introduced him.

You select groups and send them across floating lands and ship decks. Espers join as summons you recruit and group with the pirates, rather than as one limit-style call. Penelo flies with the crew instead of waiting off-screen.

Orders, movement, and abilities share one clock. A summoned Esper fights as a unit inside the formation. Losing the leader can collapse a skirmish even while the summons are still out.

Think & Feel handled the handheld battles with Square Enix. The PS2 gambit system and the long overland walk are a different game. This sequel starts after that story and moves the camera to squad command.
kirby-squeak-squad:
A treasure chest stolen by the Squeaks opens Kirby: Squeak Squad, and Kirby is sure it held his strawberry shortcake. HAL Laboratory and Flagship developed the chase, which Nintendo published in 2006. Europe calls the same cartridge Kirby: Mouse Attack.

Copy abilities can sit in a stomach inventory instead of vanishing at the next hit. On the touch screen, two stored abilities mix into a new one. The bag, not the last enemy inhaled, decides what he is carrying.

Daroach leads the thieves who ran off with the chest. The mouse-like crew keeps snatching it back. The shortcake misunderstanding is what sends Kirby after them.

Because several abilities can be stored, he can swap without hunting a fresh donor. Flagship shared the development with HAL Laboratory. Mouse Attack is a regional name, not a second quest.
another-code-two-memories:
Ashley Mizuki Robbins searches Blood Edward Island for her father in Another Code: Two Memories. Cing developed the mystery and Nintendo published it in 2005. North America retitled the same story Trace Memory.

Puzzles often split across the two screens, pairing a note or a photograph with the room in front of her. The DAS, a fictional device she carries, reads messages and triggers machines on the island. She arrives as a girl looking for a parent, not as a detective for hire.

The island is remote, with a laboratory past and a house that does not surrender its locks. Her father's absence is the reason she takes the boat. The DAS stays in the bag as both a tool and a piece of the family question.

Hotel Dusk is a different Cing mystery with a different lead. Trace Memory is not a sequel to that hotel. This island search is the earlier game.
disgaea-afternoon-of-darkness:
Laharl, Etna, and Flonne return in Disgaea: Afternoon of Darkness, a handheld port of Hour of Darkness. Nippon Ichi made the port and NIS America published the Western release in 2009. The result is extra content on an old campaign, not a new numbered sequel.

Geo panels color the grid and chain explosions when those colors line up. The Dark Assembly is the senate where bills can change rules, stats, and shop stock. Senators can be persuaded, bribed, or tossed, and a failed vote is still part of the comedy.

Laharl is the demon prince after his father's throne. Etna schemes as his vassal, and Flonne is the angel sent to watch him. Their arguing sets the tone of the maps.

The PlayStation 2 original is the Hour of Darkness campaign. This edition adds material that disc did not include. Disgaea 2 and the later numbered tales are different wars.
picross-3d:
You chisel a solid block instead of filling squares in Picross 3D. HAL Laboratory and Nintendo released that sculpting logic puzzle in 2010. Numbers on the faces tell which cubes to cut and which to leave.

One tool breaks a cube away and another marks it as solid. The figure inside may be an animal, a vehicle, or a household object once the spare cubes are gone. A wrong cut cracks the block and costs a life.

Picross DS gives you a flat grid. This puzzle rotates, and the clues wrap the faces. A row can run through depth, so a number you need may sit on a side you have not turned toward yet.

HAL Laboratory kept number logic and changed the gesture into a chisel. Nintendo published the blocks. Turning the sculpture is part of reading it, not a camera flourish.
okamiden:
Chibiterasu, a wolf pup, travels with a human partner in Okamiden. Capcom released the sequel in 2011, set after Okami. The Celestial Brush is drawn with the stylus on the lower screen.
