Strokes can still call the sun, cut a foe, or bloom a tree, carrying techniques over from the earlier tale. The pup is small enough to share the road with a child rather than running the provinces alone. Companions change as the journey moves on.

Okami followed the full-grown white wolf Amaterasu. This story follows her pup, so the gods and battles sit downstream of that first victory. You are not replaying her original journey under a shorter title.

Capcom kept the ink-wash hills and moved the brush onto the stylus. The lower screen is the paper. The upper screen is the world that ink changes.
contra-4:
Both screens stack into one tall battlefield in Contra 4, a run-and-gun WayForward built for Konami in 2007. A grappling hook climbs the seam where the displays meet. Classic Contra weapons return beside that hook.

You still run, jump, and fire through soldiers and alien guns. A hook shot or a ladder can carry you from the lower display fully onto the upper one. Familiar guns, spread patterns among them, sit in the weapon cycle.

Contra III is a different game, the Super Nintendo entry with its own stages and its own overhead sections. This mission was built for the tall view. WayForward did not paste the older cartridge onto two screens.

Konami published the result. The hook is the first movement trick to practice, because many rooms are taller than one display. A bullet that shares your tile still ends the life immediately.
super-scribblenauts:
Adjectives change what you spawn in Super Scribblenauts, so a red heavy crate is not the same object as a plain crate. 5th Cell and Warner Bros. released the sequel in 2010. An object editor lets you build a custom thing, name it, and call it back.

The first Scribblenauts game understood nouns alone. Here, color, weight, and temperament can be typed in front of the noun, and the simulation tries to honor them. A flying refrigerator and a tiny refrigerator solve different gaps.

Maxwell returns with the notebook, now listening to describing words. Starites are still the hidden goal of a level. The editor turns a favorite invention into a word you can reuse.

Warner Bros. published what 5th Cell added on top of the noun toy. If a long phrase fails, the object may appear without the trait you wanted. A shorter adjective is the better test before you stack five of them.
advance-wars-days-of-ruin:
A meteor disaster replaces the bright Wars World in Advance Wars: Days of Ruin, and a new cast fights in the ruins. Intelligent Systems developed the campaign and Nintendo published it in 2008. Europe received the same war as Advance Wars: Dark Conflict.

Andy and the cheerful commanding officers of the older games do not lead these armies. Shortages and ruined cities keep the writing harsh. CO powers still charge as units fight, then tip a battle when they are spent.

Units still move on a grid, capture properties, and spend funds. The meteor is why the map looks abandoned rather than festive. New officers carry the powers, and their personalities are not the old cartoon roster.

Dark Conflict is a regional title, not a second campaign. Intelligent Systems kept the grid and removed the sunny framing. Tank spacing and infantry still decide the turn.
pokemon-conquest:
Warlords and Pokémon share the region of Ransei in Pokémon Conquest, a crossover with Nobunaga's Ambition. Koei Tecmo and Nintendo released the campaign in 2012. You link a warrior to a Pokémon and fight for territory.

Each warlord bonds with a partner, and the link can deepen until the pair acts as one unit. Kingdoms change hands when armies meet. There is no gym circuit and no league from the main series.

Nobunaga's Ambition supplies banners, castles, and a famous unifier as the looming rival. The creatures supply the ranks those warlords send forward. A warrior without a linked partner is not the unit the battles expect.

Koei Tecmo built the tactics, and Nintendo published them. Between fights you recruit warriors and match them to partners. Badge quests belong on other cartridges.
kirby-mass-attack:
Up to ten small Kirbys swarm the levels of Kirby Mass Attack, and you flick them with the stylus. HAL Laboratory developed the crowd, which Nintendo published in 2011. They gang up on enemies instead of swallowing a copy ability.

A flick sends the group running that way. They pile onto a foe, weigh down a switch, or boost one another toward a high ledge. Lose too many bodies and the remainder cannot lift the same obstacles.

Necrodeus shatters one Kirby into this handful. The number of Kirbys is the resource that matters. Fruit and rescued friends push that number back toward the cap of ten.

HAL Laboratory built the stages around touch flicks rather than around a power you inhale. Nintendo published the cartridge. Treat the crowd as one cursor with many feet.
shin-megami-tensei-devil-survivor:
Tokyo is locked down in Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Survivor, and a death clock on your phone counts the days you have left. Atlus released this DS original in 2009. Demons are bought at auction and then fielded in tactical battles.

Quarantine walls hold people inside a city that is coming apart. The clock is a number on the device in your hand, and other people can see their own counts. When a count hits zero, that person's story ends.

Auctions trade demons for currency, and deals sit alongside the bidding. Human friends and their summoned demons share turn-based fights on a grid. The crisis is measured in days, not in an open countryside.

Overclocked, on a later handheld, is a remake with extra story material. The original lockdown, death clock and all, is the DS game. Atlus told that week there before any expanded retelling.
space-invaders-extreme:
Stages react to the music in Space Invaders Extreme, the 2008 Taito release that treats the fleet as something a soundtrack can trigger. Fever, lasers, and ships unknown to the 1978 cabinet fill the screen. Backbone helped some versions, while this DS game is Taito's music-linked Invaders.

Color matches and chains feed a fever state in which the weapons and the backdrop change. Hits answer the beat instead of sitting under unrelated music. A laser or a special ship can clear a formation the plain cannon cannot.

The old cabinet marched one fleet down a black field. Here the formations break into patterns tied to tracks, with bonus waves that do not resemble that march. You still move along the bottom and shoot upward.

The DS edition is Taito's own music-linked set. Copies on other hardware that Backbone touched are separate builds. The shift into fever is the moment a stage changes shape.
dragon-quest-v-hand-of-the-heavenly-brid:
You guide the hero as a child, an adult, and a father in Dragon Quest V: Hand of the Heavenly Bride. ArtePiazza and Square Enix rebuilt the Super Famicom game for DS in 2009. A marriage choice decides who stands with him, and monsters can join the party.

Early chapters follow a boy traveling with his father. Later chapters age him into a husband and then a parent, and the plot continues through that family. The bride is not a cosmetic portrait; the line of the story follows her.

Creatures recruited in the field take battle slots beside human allies. That recruitment is a signature of this tale, the middle story of the Zenithian trilogy. The fourth Dragon Quest comes before it, and the sixth comes after.

The DS rebuild keeps those three ages and presents them with newer illustrations. ArtePiazza worked with Square Enix on the remake. The father he becomes is the reason the childhood chapters exist.
shin-megami-tensei-strange-journey:
An armored suit replaces the usual Tokyo teenager in Shin Megami Tensei: Strange Journey. Atlus and Lancarse sent a strike team into the Schwarzwelt in 2010. That void hangs over Antarctica, and the expedition goes inside.

Demon fusion and alignment decide who fights beside you and how the ending falls. Law, chaos, and a neutral route diverge as the team argues about the sphere. The suit is life support and armor, not a school uniform.

Corridors are first-person and stepped, with demons striking out of the dark. Fusion spends two demons to produce another. Alignment moves when you answer people, not when you tick a box before the crawl.

Redux is a later remake with added material. The armored expedition through the Schwarzwelt is the original DS descent. Lancarse worked with Atlus on that first trip into the ice.
mega-man-zx:
Choose Vent or Aile, then Megamerge, in Mega Man ZX. Inti Creates developed the game and Capcom published it in 2006. Model X and Model Z are the Biometals that define the opening transformation.

Megamerge armors the chosen hero and changes the weapon in hand. Vent and Aile are the male and female leads, sharing a path with differences in the scenes around them. The setting comes after the Zero series, among humans and reploids living in the aftermath.

The Zero quartet is about Zero himself. This story starts later and puts Model Z in someone else's hands. You are not playing as Zero under a renamed title.

Inti Creates carried side-view runs forward into this new pair of heroes. Capcom published the cartridge. Further Biometals appear beyond the first two, so the opening merge is not the whole set.
resident-evil-deadly-silence:
The Spencer mansion returns in Resident Evil: Deadly Silence, and knife attacks are flicked on the touch screen. Capcom released the DS remake in 2006. Chris Redfield and Jill Valentine are still the investigators in those halls.

Rebirth mode rearranges rooms and item placement, so memory of the original mansion is not a map. Classic mode stays closer to the original layout and the original shocks. The stylus knife is a close weapon in the corridors.

Locked doors, scarce ammo, and ink-ribbon saves still structure the night. The portrait hall, the dining room, and the residence remain the geography. Caution is the pace the item counts enforce.

Resident Evil 4 is a different outbreak in a different country, with a merchant in the safe rooms. Capcom aimed this cartridge at the first mansion. Classic keeps the familiar route, and Rebirth moves the rooms.
tetris-ds:
Nintendo sets falling blocks against scenes from Mario, Zelda, Metroid, and Donkey Kong in Tetris DS. The cartridge arrived in 2006 with several ways to play. Touch push, versus matches, and mission lists sit beside a standard well.

Touch push lets the stylus shove a piece rather than only rotating it with buttons. Versus mode throws your clears at another player. Mission mode asks for particular shapes and timings instead of an endless stack.

A Mario backdrop, a Zelda scene, a Metroid corridor, or Donkey Kong girders can sit behind the same pieces. The tetrominoes do not change shape when the scenery changes. The mode you picked, and the music around the well, is what changes.

This is not the Game Boy version of Tetris. Nintendo built new modes around familiar series art. A filled standard well still ends the run.
henry-hatsworth-in-the-puzzling-adventur:
A gentleman with a tea meter fights on the upper screen of Henry Hatsworth in the Puzzling Adventure, while a match puzzle below feeds his power. EA Tiburon released that paired duel in 2009. The puzzle is the ammunition.

Matching tiles on the bottom fills the tea meter. Spending the meter strengthens his attacks above, up to a frantic tea-powered state. Ignore the puzzle and he is left with a weaker strike.

Foes beaten on top can fall into the puzzle as blocks that must be cleared. The two screens are one fight. A clogged board is as dangerous as a lost hit point.

EA Tiburon built both halves. Raise the meter before a crowded room, because puzzle clears are what make the upper attacks worth using. Manners do not swing the damage; the tea does.
etrian-odyssey:
You draw the map on the lower screen in Etrian Odyssey while the upper screen shows a first-person corridor of the Yggdrasil labyrinth. Atlus released this first Etrian in 2007. FOEs patrol as powerful enemies marked on the chart you are sketching.

Walls, doors, and icons go down in your own hand. A blank chart is a real choice, and a careful one separates a safe stair from a dead end. The guild you name is the party taking those jobs.

FOEs are often too strong to kill on the floor where you first see their mark. Walking around them is a valid plan. Yggdrasil's labyrinth is the whole theme, floor after floor.

Later sequels add other lands and other rules. This cartridge is the original guild under the original tree. Atlus expected the pencil to move every time you take a step.
electroplankton:
Electroplankton is a music toy, an interactive album by Toshio Iwai that Nintendo published in 2006. There is no score to beat and no stage to clear. The creatures answer the microphone, the stylus, and the closing of the lid.

Hanenbow sends bouncing bodies across leaves, and the angle of a leaf changes the note. Tracy follows lines you draw and leaves a glowing path of sound. Lumiloop is a set of rings you spin so tones can stack.

Other creatures in the set listen for a voice or a clap, and one of them answers when the lid shuts. You perform a piece rather than win it. Iwai designed them as instruments.

Nintendo published the album as a cartridge played by touch and noise. A favorite creature is worth revisiting, because there is no final boss to reach. Silence, a hard tap, or a shut lid can all change the piece.
clubhouse-games:
Cards, darts, billiards, and board games share Clubhouse Games, and the Japanese box reads 42 All-Time Classics. Agenda developed the collection and Nintendo published it in 2006. A friend can join a match from that one cartridge.

The Japanese name states the count: forty-two tables, decks, and boards. Darts and billiards sit beside card games and classic boards. You pick a ruleset and play a match.

On a supported game, a second player can enter without bringing another copy. That single-cartridge multiplayer is how a visitor takes a side. The rules still come from the cartridge in the first machine.

Agenda assembled the rule set. Nintendo published the compilation. The menu is wide on purpose, a clubhouse of short matches rather than one deep season.
radiant-historia:
Stocke, an agent of history, weaves two timelines at nodes in Radiant Historia. Atlus released the DS original in 2011, with music by Yoko Shimomura. In battle you push enemies onto one tile so a follow-up can hit the stack.

The timelines are different versions of the same war. A node is a moment where Stocke can cross over and change a choice, then return if that path dies. The history he guards is his job.

Knocking foes into the same square sets up a heavier blow. Where they stand matters more than a static row of fighters. Allies fill the party while he decides which history to repair.

Perfect Chronology is a later remake on another system. Stocke's nodes and Shimomura's score were first heard together on the DS original. Atlus published that first telling.
dragon-quest-monsters-joker:
Scout a monster, ride one, and enter a tournament in Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker. Square Enix restarted the monsters line on DS with this 2007 game. It is not Dragon Warrior Monsters 2.

Scouting is how a wild creature joins after a fight, under rules that are stricter than a simple knockout. Riding a large monster changes travel on the field. The tournament gives the road a bracket and a rival.

Older Dragon Warrior Monsters cartridges are the ancestors, and the second of them is its own game. This restart uses a new hero and a new circuit of islands. Square Enix treated it as a fresh start.

Rank and breeding matter once the stable grows. The mount you ride can also be sent into a fight. Tournament rounds are how the story measures a scout.
diddy-kong-racing-ds:
Planes, hovercraft, and cars share the cups of Diddy Kong Racing DS. Rare rebuilt the N64 racer, and Nintendo published the DS edition in 2007. New tracks, touch-screen gimmicks, and Taj set it apart from the television original.

You still choose land, water, or air and race themed courses in that vehicle. Stylus gimmicks add moments the older version never asked for. Extra tracks push the cup list past the original layout.

Taj, the genie associated with the challenges, is part of this edition. Diddy remains the face on the box. Rare retuned the handling for the two small screens.

The N64 racer has its own page, and so does Mario Kart DS. Neither is this remake. Taj and the added courses are the quickest way to tell the handheld edition from the older Diddy meet.
rune-factory-2-a-fantasy-harvest-moon:
You live as a parent and later as that parent's child in Rune Factory 2: A Fantasy Harvest Moon. Neverland developed the generation shift, and Natsume published it in the United States in 2008. Farm work and dungeon floors share the same days.

The first generation tills, befriends the town, and delves. After the story turns, control passes to the child, who inherits the fields and a further plot. The child is the second half of this game, not a bonus file.

Seeds, seasons, and monster-filled caves are the daily mix. A failed crop costs the season. A bad floor costs the afternoon and the supplies you carried in.

Rune Factory 4 is a later entry with another hero and another town. Neverland's second game is the parent-and-child tale. The child's tools and the parent's unfinished fields are the handoff between those halves.
last-window-the-secret-of-cape-west:
Kyle Hyde takes another case in Last Window: The Secret of Cape West, Cing's sequel to Hotel Dusk. Nintendo published the mystery in 2010. Cape West was a hotel and now stands as the apartment house where he lives.

The investigation is point-and-click on the two screens. You examine objects, question residents, and keep track of what they hide. Hyde, a former detective working as a salesman, still cannot leave old deaths alone.

This was the last game Cing finished. No later title came out of the studio after it. Conversation and a slow search of one building carry the case.

Europe received a standalone English DS release. North America did not get a standalone English DS release. That split is a fact about the published editions.
solatorobo-red-the-hunter:
Red, a dog-like hunter, crews an airship in Solatorobo: Red the Hunter. CyberConnect2 developed the adventure, and XSEED published it in the west in 2011. Trance form is the heightened state he enters when a fight outgrows his usual swings.

The floating world is the same one Tail Concerto used, populated by animal people and airships. Hunter jobs send the ship between islands. Trance changes his body and his strength for a limited burst.

Platform jumping fills the ruins, and the ship covers the distance between them. Towns perched on scraps of land hand out the work. Elh travels with him in the cockpit while Red is the body you move in a scrap.

CyberConnect2 tied the hunter story to that older world without asking you to replay Tail Concerto. XSEED handled the Western release. Trance spends a gauge, so the transformation is a burst rather than a permanent suit.
the-dark-spire:
A party of adventurers you name enters a first-person maze in The Dark Spire, built in the Wizardry tradition. Success developed it, and Atlus published the United States release in 2009. A wireframe option can strip the walls down to lines.

You assign classes and step tile by tile. The maze does not illustrate itself the way a hand-drawn chart would. Encounters arrive in first person, and a bad fight can end the delve.

Wizardry is the ancestor: grid, darkness, and a party that can fail. Etrian Odyssey is a different series, one in which you sketch the map yourself. This tower is not that sketchbook.

Atlus brought Success's maze to American shelves. The names you type are the only identities the adventurers have. The wireframe view is optional for players who want the older line-drawn look.
the-legendary-starfy:
Swim, spin, and ride animal friends in The Legendary Starfy, the first Starfy game released in the West. Tose developed it and Nintendo published it in 2008. Japan already knew this story as the fifth Densetsu no Stafi.

The hero is a starfish prince. Spin attacks and swimming strokes are how he moves. A ridden animal changes the current of a stage, carrying him through water he would cross slowly alone.

Moe the clam tags along and talks. Courses mix open water, dry ground, and creatures large enough to board. The tone stays light.

Four earlier Densetsu no Stafi games stayed in Japan. Tose and Nintendo brought this fifth one across. It is not a Kirby game, even though both are bright side-view adventures.
evo-search-for-eden:
A fish eats its way up the tree of life in E.V.O.: Search for Eden, spending points on jaws, legs, and horns. Givro and Almanic developed the side-scroller, and Enix published it in 1992. It is an evolution journey on the Super Nintendo, not a menu-driven role-playing game.

You scroll through successive eras, bite other creatures, and bank evolution points. Those points buy body parts that change the bite and the gait. A jaw may come before a leg, and a horn may wait until the frame can carry it.

Later stretches leave the water. The same creature continues, rebuilt, instead of handing you a new hero at a town gate. There is no equipment shop, because the body is the equipment.

Enix published the Givro and Almanic experiment. The scrolling fight and the edible landscape are the whole loop. Grow a body that matches the era, or get eaten by it.
metal-warriors:
You can eject from your machine and hijack an enemy one in Metal Warriors. LucasArts developed the side-view missions, and Konami published them in 1995. On foot, the pilot is small enough to climb into another cockpit.

A captured frame brings its own guns and its own jump. Staying inside the starting mech ignores the tool the stages keep offering. The pilot outside the armor is fragile beside the machines.

LucasArts and Konami are an unusual pairing on a Super Nintendo box. One developed the missions and the other published them. The side view makes rooftops and jumps part of the shooting.

Learn which enemy frames are worth stealing. Their weapons are not clones of yours. The hijack is the reason to leave the cockpit at all.
disneys-magical-quest:
Mickey Mouse changes costume in Disney's Magical Quest, Capcom's first platform game in that series, released in 1992. A firefighter outfit, a mountain-climber outfit, and, in later forms, a magician's clothes each grant a different move. It is not the third quest.

The firefighter's hose climbs and strikes. The climber's gear answers vertical shafts. The magician form arrives later and changes the attack again.

Emperor Pete sets the chase in motion by kidnapping Pluto. Mickey puts the costumes on to get him back. Capcom draws him so the outfit reads clearly against the stage.

Later sequels add more characters and more worlds. This opening game stays with Mickey and the costume line. Capcom's Disney platform work of that period starts with these outfits.
sparkster:
An opossum with a jet pack and a sword stars in Sparkster, Konami's Super Nintendo Rocket Knight game from 1994. He dashes on the pack, rebounds, and cuts with the blade. The Genesis cartridge that uses the same name, from the same era, is a different design.

Rocket Knight is his role, not a second hero standing next to him. Stages are side-view speed courses, and the pack is both travel and attack. The sword covers the space the burst does not.

Konami did not ship one identical layout on both 16-bit machines. Bosses and level ideas on the Super Nintendo diverge from the Genesis design. Treat the two as siblings rather than as a matched pair.

The pack's burst is the move to master, because distance and damage both come out of it. The armored opossum is the only lead. Super Nintendo bursts and sword routes are this layout, not the Genesis one.
super-bomberman-5:
A world map links the stages of Super Bomberman 5, Hudson Soft's Japan-only Super Famicom release from 1997. It is the last main Super Bomberman on that console. Official publication stayed in Japan.

You move on the map and enter stages in an order the battle-only boxes did not emphasize. Bombs, blasts, and brick still decide each room. The map gives the single-player route a shape.

This is not Super Bomberman 2, an earlier and separate entry. Hudson Soft kept the fifth game on the Super Famicom. Western shops did not get an official box for it.

Multiplayer battles remain available beside the mapped route. New tiles show up as the map progresses. Hudson Soft closed the main line on that console with this release.
super-bomberman-4:
Bomberman characters ride animals in the story mode of Super Bomberman 4, Hudson Soft's 1996 game for the Japanese Super Famicom. Multiplayer remains the heart of the cartridge. It is not the first Super Bomberman.

Story stages put riders on creatures that change how a maze is crossed. The animals are mounts inside the bomb rules, not a separate race. Cast members fill the story roles.

Battle rounds are still why players gather around one machine. Grids, bombs, and sudden traps decide those rounds. The mounted story is a path around that table, not a replacement for it.

Hudson Soft aimed the fourth Super Famicom entry at both the animal rides and the usual bouts. Earlier games in the line had already established the battles. The original box is a different, earlier release.
the-king-of-dragons:
Choose a fighter, a cleric, an elf, a wizard, or a dwarf in The King of Dragons. Capcom's 1991 arcade brawler later reached home as a port, and a red dragon threatens the kingdom. Two players can march through the horde together.

The fighter stays close, the elf strikes from farther out, and the wizard and cleric lean on spells while the dwarf holds a stout line. The calling is chosen before the road starts. Side by side, two classes cover gaps one class leaves open.

Smaller monsters fill the road before the red dragon. The threat to the kingdom is that dragon, not a random late reptile. Side-view waves show the coin-op origins.

The home port keeps the class select and the cooperative brawling. Five callings are the whole roster of roles. Pick for range, then stay near a partner when the screen fills.
warios-woods-1994:
Toad drops bombs on monsters while Wario floods the forest in Wario's Woods (1994). Nintendo made this Super Nintendo puzzle. Toad's bomb-stacking is the fight on that cartridge.

Bombs fall into a pit of creatures, and Toad arranges them so a blast clears the stack. Wario keeps sending more monsters down. Timer pressure and rising clutter are the whole round.

You play as Toad. Wario is the one stuffing the woods with enemies, not the hands you control. Clear a stack before the next wave lands on it.

The NES edition is a different release, and it was the last licensed game on that console. Toad still stacks bombs on the Super Nintendo cartridge. Wario's flood of monsters is the pressure on that forest board.
norse-by-norse-west-the-return-of-the-lo:
Erik, Baleog, and Olaf return with new skills in Norse by Norse West: The Return of the Lost Vikings. The long name is the United States title of Lost Vikings 2, published in 1997. Silicon & Synapse (Blizzard) and Beam Software developed it, and Interplay published it.

Each viking still solves a different part of a room. Erik's bulk, Baleog's weapons, and Olaf's shield come back, then gain tricks the first quest did not teach. You swap among the three to move one room forward.

American boxes use the long Norse title rather than a short numeral alone. Interplay put the cartridge out. Silicon & Synapse, named in the credit as Blizzard, shared the work with Beam Software.

A new skill is why a familiar viking can cross a gap that used to stop him. Try the viking who looks wrong for a ledge before you decide the route is blocked. The rooms expect those added tricks.
knights-of-the-round:
Arthur, Lancelot, and Percival fight as a team in Knights of the Round, Capcom's arcade port from 1991. Horses carry them in some sections. It is not The King of Dragons.

The three knights differ in reach and power, and three players can take them together. On foot they clear crowds with swords. Mounted stretches change the speed and the spacing of those swings.

The other Capcom coin-op lets each player pick a fantasy calling and march against a red dragon. This Arthurian road puts the knights on horseback for part of the march. Those two ports are not interchangeable.

Mounted sections survive in the home version rather than vanishing into a sidewalk fight. Know which knight you hold before companions fill the other seats. Percival is not a recolor of Arthur.
clayfighter:
Blob, Ickybod Clay, and Bad Mr. Frosty fight in ClayFighter, the 1993 Super Nintendo comedy bout from Visual Concepts, Ringler Studios, and Interplay. The figures look like photographed clay. It is not Street Fighter.

Mushy outlines and joke specials are the point of the roster. Bad Mr. Frosty brings a snowman kit, Blob wobbles through grabs, and Ickybod Clay plays the ghost. The remaining fighters stay in that same silly material.

Interplay published the cartridge. Visual Concepts and Ringler Studios built the digitized clay. Damage exists, and so do the gags in the poses.

Serious tournament shotos belong to a different series. A snowman's throw is a normal part of this cast. Pick a clay body for the gag, then learn the move that gag is hiding.
super-double-dragon:
Billy and Jimmy Lee bring a move set unlike their NES outings to Super Double Dragon, including a charge attack. Technos released the Super Nintendo revision in 1992. It is not Double Dragon II.

The brothers still fight side by side through street gangs. The charge winds up a heavier blow than the quick punches. Throws and kicks join that charge in a list the NES pads did not share.

Double Dragon II has its own stages and its own identity. Technos rebuilt the moves for the 16-bit machine rather than tracing the older patterns. Players who only know the NES buttons will miss the charge unless they practice it.

Both brothers can use the expanded list. The charge has to come out under pressure, not only in an empty alley. Technos kept their names and changed the fighting underneath.
un-squadron:
Shin Kazama flies for a mercenary air force in U.N. Squadron, Capcom's side-scrolling shooter based on the manga Area 88. You pick a pilot and buy planes with mission pay on this 1991 Super Nintendo release. The airfield belongs to hired guns, not to a national parade.

Each pilot handles differently, so the seat you choose changes the sortie. Money from a clear can buy a faster airframe or a stronger gun. Area 88 supplies the premise: pilots who fight for pay in someone else's war.

Shin Kazama is the central pilot from that manga, and he is one of the selectable seats. Other aces fill the remaining choices. The shop between missions matters as much as the dodge pattern in the air.

Capcom built both the scrolling attacks and the purchase loop. The plane you bought is the build you bring to the next wave. Readers of the manga will know the mercenary squadron; the shop explains itself either way.
mega-lo-mania:
Research runs from sticks to lasers in Mega Lo Mania, then you send followers to fight. Sensible Software made the god game and Virgin published it in 1991. Some Western boxes call the same game Tyrants: Fight Through Time.

Islands are taken in sequence. Followers assigned to huts research the next weapon and then march with it. A stick-armed band loses to a later island that has already reached guns.

You are not a soldier on the field. You are the planner deciding how many people study, how many build, and how many attack. The tech ladder is the clock.

Sensible Software designed that escalation. Virgin published the Super Nintendo edition. Tyrants: Fight Through Time is an alternate title on certain boxes, not a second ruleset.
